cards.power: Objection! Play this card to demand a player cite a non-existent rule. If they hesitate, their action fails.
cards.lore: Dry leader. Busy.

cards.power: Efficiency Protocol: You may reroll a die, but your story narration must be devoid of fun or flavor.
cards.lore: Nothing breaks faster than trying to weaponize ambiguity.

cards.power: Panic Check: Ask “Is this right?” If anyone answers “Yes,” discard this card and ignore the consequence.
cards.lore: Confusing clarity with safety.

cards.power: The Meta: Cancel a move that is “too fun” on the grounds that it isn’t optimal.
cards.lore: Authority sneaks back in wearing a helpful voice.

cards.power: Internal Scream: If a die rolls off the table, you must freeze until someone tells you it's okay.
cards.lore: For those who freeze when meaning is not externally validated.

cards.power: Dependency: You cannot take an Action unless another player gives you permission first.
cards.lore: Stabilize play when certainty becomes a crutch.

cards.power: Slippery Dice: Reroll any 6. You cannot handle success without questioning it.
cards.lore: Others start sweating. This booklet is for them.

cards.power: The Void: Play when the table stalls. Silence counts as a valid turn.
cards.lore: A controlled void. A moment where players stop asking.

cards.power: Forfeit: Give this card to anyone discussing “Victory Points.” They lose their next turn.
cards.lore: Whoever asks how to win has already lost.

cards.power: Valid Move: Play to justify an action that defies logic but feels right.
cards.lore: Blödsinn is not a mistake. It is a state.

cards.power: Pragmatism: Ignore a rule if the result creates a better story.
cards.lore: Nobody is right. Some things are effective.

cards.power: Reset: Ignore the precedent set by the previous turn. We start fresh.
cards.lore: The game remembers nothing. The players do.

cards.power: Argument Ender: Play to instantly win a meta-argument about rules interpretation.
cards.lore: Cry harder, Esq.

cards.power: Reality Check: If the table laughs, your roll succeeds automatically.
cards.lore: If it makes no sense, it may be correct.

cards.power: Venting: Stop the game. Everyone takes a deep breath. No game state changes.
cards.lore: They exist to interrupt pure panic.

cards.power: Simplification: Remove one constraint from the current Scene.
cards.lore: If you need more rules, you may use fewer.

cards.power: Edit: Physically cross out one word on a Stage Card. It is now forever removed.
cards.lore: Hand-written rule lists and crossed-out instructions.

cards.power: Revision: Change the Quest Goal immediately after the dice are rolled.
cards.lore: Documents labeled “FINAL” and immediately contradicted.

cards.power: Validation: Play to approve a move that the “Rules Lawyer” rejected.
cards.lore: Fake approval stamps.

cards.power: Loophole: Avoid a consequence by claiming you read the fine print.
cards.lore: Pseudo-legal disclaimers.

cards.power: Declaration: Read the Anti-Rule aloud. No discussion allowed.
cards.lore: As a Table Declaration.

cards.power: Absence: Remove a card from the Stage. Replace it with nothing. Narrate the gap.
cards.lore: A deliberate absence of authority.

cards.power: Focus: If everyone looks at you, +1 to your roll.
cards.lore: Re-anchor play in shared attention instead of correctness.

cards.power: Risk: Ask “Safer from what?” If nobody answers, take a token.
cards.lore: If a rule makes you feel safer, ask yourself: Safer from what?

cards.power: Tension Break: Play when someone laughs nervously. You both draw a card.
cards.lore: Someone laughs nervously. This indicates correct operation.

cards.power: Critique: Claim this is “Bad Design,” reroll your die.
cards.lore: Someone claims this is bad design.

cards.power: Intervention: Play when the table stalls. The Anti-Rule stands in the room like a smell.
cards.lore: When the table stalls… invoke an Anti-Rule.

cards.power: Stop: Any player may play this to stop trying to win. They are now telling stories.
cards.lore: Someone stops trying to win.

cards.power: Restriction: Force a player to use simple words only.
cards.lore: A compliance aid for people who hate improvisation.

cards.power: Comfort: Protect an Actor from a “Blödsinn” check.
cards.lore: For players who need rules to feel safe.

cards.power: Vibes: Play this card. It does nothing. If it bothers someone, you gain a token.
cards.lore: These feelings are ironic.

cards.power: Presentation: Stand up and explain your move like a CEO. If they buy it, it works.
cards.lore: Belong in marketing, slides, posters, and onboarding jokes.

cards.power: Reveal: Point at the player who is actually leading the table. They must skip a turn.
cards.lore: Expose hidden power dynamics at the table.

cards.power: Doubt: Challenge a “correct” move. There is no correct move.
cards.lore: Remove the illusion of a “correct” move.

cards.power: Deflect: Shift the consequence of a bad roll to the Game Designer.
cards.lore: Look for someone to blame.

cards.power: Define: You decide what another player's card “really” means.
cards.lore: Look for the correct interpretation.

cards.power: Witness: Do nothing. Just observe. Your silence is a valid move.
cards.lore: Plants in pots. Silent visual gags.

cards.power: Paperwork: Demand a player mime filling out a form before rolling.
cards.lore: Philosophers, clerks, editors. Bureaucrats.

cards.power: Snapshot: Remember the current board state. You may revert to it later.
cards.lore: Bizarre aliens. Surreal creatures.

cards.power: Anarchy: Destroy this card (rip it up). Rewrite one rule for the rest of the game.
cards.lore: Analog-first DIY cut&play artist.

cards.power: Roleplay: Wear it (mime). You are in charge until you laugh.
cards.lore: Allow law-and-order players to stay.

cards.power: Policing: If you catch someone optimizing, you get a token.
cards.lore: Default to policing or rule-lawyering.

cards.power: Explanation: Explain the “Science” of your move to gain a bonus.
cards.lore: The table is encouraged to let them try.

cards.power: Humility: Wear it if you ask for a rule clarification. It protects you from judgment.
cards.lore: Make rule anxiety visible without punishing it.

cards.power: Interpretation: The rules mean whatever the group decides they mean tonight.
cards.lore: They look for the designer's intent.

cards.power: Obscure: Play on another card. That card's text is now open to interpretation.
cards.lore: Most games collapse under ambiguity.

cards.power: Betrayal: Break a promise made in a previous turn for narrative effect.
cards.lore: Determine responsibility.

cards.power: Reset: Pull to end the Scene immediately if it gets boring.
cards.lore: Leave the emergency handle named “Please tell me the correct move” unused.

cards.power: Shift: Force an Actor to change their MOOD to “anxious.”
cards.lore: MOOD: The emotional state driving your Actor.

cards.power: Incompetence: An Actor forgets their SKILL for this scene.
cards.lore: SKILL: The trained ability your Actor relies on.

cards.power: Tip: Instantly change the Quest Goal by 1/2.
cards.lore: If the tips, Quest collapses.

cards.power: Disconnect: Interrupt a story connection that feels forced.
cards.lore: Tell a story connecting Mood → Stage → Quest.

cards.power: Game Over: End the game if everyone at the table feels “fluffy” (relaxed/confused).
cards.lore: Stay Fluffy.

cards.power: Victory: Win the game instantly if you shout “BINGO!” for no reason.
cards.lore: Kayfabingo!

cards.power: Awareness: +1 to rolls if you are visibly uncomfortable.
cards.lore: Uncomfortable, irritated, or strangely alert.

cards.power: Consensus: The group decides when it is done. No winner.
cards.lore: When the group feels done.
